subject: Logic
title: Laplace's Demon
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Laplace's Demon.

hook.text: If a mind knew the position and velocity of every atom, could it predict the entire future? Laplace said yes.

buildup.text: In 1814, Laplace imagined an intellect vast enough to compute every future event from present conditions.

discovery.text: Under classical physics, the universe is deterministic—every future state follows inevitably from the present.

twist.text: Quantum mechanics shattered this. Some events are fundamentally random—no data predicts which atom decays next.

climax.text: Even chaos theory limits prediction: tiny measurement errors explode into massive forecast failures over time.

punchline.text: The universe keeps secrets even from omniscience.

quiz.question: What undermined Laplace's demon?
options: Quantum randomness and chaotic sensitivity to initial conditions
